title: Boss: the login service
summary: Put hashing, verification, TOTP and throttling together into a login service.

steps.title: The login service
body: You are building the core of a login system that a web API will call. Three pieces, each tested on its own, and then the whole thing:
1. A password hasher that makes its own salts.
2. A TOTP verifier that tolerates clock drift but refuses replays.
3. A login service that ties hashing, MFA and throttling together without leaking which accounts exist.
Everything takes time as a parameter. No `DateTime.Now`.

steps.title: A password hasher
prompt: Write a static class `PasswordHasher` with the methods below. The tests already import `System.Security.Cryptography`, so don't add `using` lines.

- `static string Hash(string password, int iterations)`: makes a fresh 16-byte salt with `RandomNumberGenerator` and returns `pbkdf2-sha256$<iterations>$<salt b64>$<hash b64>` (PBKDF2-SHA256, 32-byte hash).
- `static bool Verify(string password, string stored)`: as in the lesson, constant-time, `false` for malformed input.
Hashing the same password twice must give two different strings, and both must verify.
starter: public static string Hash(string password, int iterations) => "";
public static bool Verify(string password, string stored) => false;
solution: public static string Hash(string password, int iterations)
byte[] hash = Rfc2898DeriveBytes.Pbkdf2(password, salt, iterations, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256, 32);
public static bool Verify(string password, string stored)
if (!int.TryParse(parts[1], out int iterations) || iterations < 1) return false;
byte[] actual = Rfc2898DeriveBytes.Pbkdf2(password, salt, iterations, HashAlgorithmName.SHA256, expected.Length);
hints: Reuse your `Verify` from the lesson, guarding the parse with `int.TryParse`.
template: Dojo.Check("the result has the pbkdf2-sha256$1000$ prefix", dojoA.StartsWith("pbkdf2-sha256$1000$"), dojoA);
Dojo.Check("two hashes of the same password differ", dojoA != dojoB, "both were " + dojoA);
Dojo.Eq("the first hash verifies", true, PasswordHasher.Verify("s3cret-pass", dojoA));
Dojo.Eq("the second hash verifies", true, PasswordHasher.Verify("s3cret-pass", dojoB));
Dojo.Eq("a wrong password does not verify", false, PasswordHasher.Verify("s3cret-pasS", dojoA));
Dojo.Eq("a known stored value verifies", true, PasswordHasher.Verify("correct horse", "pbkdf2-sha256$1000$AAECAwQFBgcICQoLDA0ODw==$yRTMTwbMbo9G0VfjobWqerzuuxe7BETNTErBbKKumGQ="));
Dojo.Eq("a malformed value is rejected", false, PasswordHasher.Verify("x", "pbkdf2-sha256$abc"));

steps.title: Drift-tolerant, replay-proof TOTP
prompt: Write a class `TotpVerifier`:
- Constructor `TotpVerifier(byte[] secret)`.

- `bool Verify(string code, long unixSeconds)`: `true` when `code` equals the 6-digit TOTP for the current 30-second window **or the one before or after it**. Once a code for some window has been accepted, reject any code for that window **or any earlier window** (that stops replay).

You will need your `Totp` function from the lesson inside the class (as a private method). Compare codes with `CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals` on their bytes. `System.Security.Cryptography` is already imported by the tests.
With the RFC secret `12345678901234567890`: time 59 is window 1 with code `287082`.
starter: public bool Verify(string code, long unixSeconds) => false;
solution: public bool Verify(string code, long unixSeconds)
for (long w = now - 1; w <= now + 1; w++)
hints: Keep a `_lastUsed` window field and skip any window `<= _lastUsed`.
Set `_lastUsed` to the window that matched before returning `true`.
template: Dojo.Eq("a wrong code is rejected", false, dojoV.Verify("000000", 59));
Dojo.Eq("the code for window 1 is accepted at time 59", true, dojoV.Verify("287082", 59));
Dojo.Eq("the same code is not accepted twice", false, dojoV.Verify("287082", 60));
Dojo.Eq("a code from the previous window is accepted (clock drift)", true, dojoV2.Verify("287082", 75));
Dojo.Eq("a code from two windows ago is rejected", false, dojoV3.Verify("287082", 95));
Dojo.Eq("8-digit RFC code checked at time 1111111109 (6 digits: 081804)", true, dojoV4.Verify("081804", 1111111109));
Dojo.Eq("an earlier window is rejected after a later one was used", false, dojoV4.Verify("287082", 59));

steps.title: The login service
prompt: Write a class `LoginService` that answers a login attempt with one of four strings.
```csharp
var svc = new LoginService(maxFailures: 3, window: TimeSpan.FromMinutes(15));
svc.AddUser("ada", storedHash, totpSecret: null);       // password only
svc.AddUser("grace", storedHash2, totpSecret: secret);  // password + TOTP
string result = svc.Login("ada", "pw", totp: null, now);
`Login(string user, string password, string? totp, DateTimeOffset now)` returns:
1. `"locked"` if the user has `maxFailures` or more failures inside the window (check this **first**, before the password).
2. `"invalid"` if the user does not exist or the password is wrong. Record a failure **for that username even when it doesn't exist**, so attackers can't tell the difference.
3. `"mfa_required"` if the password is right, the user has a TOTP secret, and `totp` is `null` or wrong. A wrong code counts as a failure; a missing one does not.
4. `"ok"` otherwise, and the user's failures are cleared.

For TOTP use 6 digits and the current window only (`now.ToUnixTimeSeconds()`). The tests provide `PasswordHasher.Verify(password, stored)` and `Otp.Totp(byte[] secret, long unixSeconds, int digits)` for you to call; you write `LoginService`.

public string Login(string user, string password, string? totp, DateTimeOffset now) => "invalid";

public string Login(string user, string password, string? totp, DateTimeOffset now)
private bool IsLocked(string user, DateTimeOffset now) =>
_failures.TryGetValue(user, out var list) && list.Count(t => now - t < _window) >= _max;
private void Fail(string user, DateTimeOffset now)
if (!_failures.TryGetValue(user, out var list)) _failures[user] = list = new();
hints: Keep two dictionaries: users (hash + optional secret) and failure times per username.
Order matters: locked check, then password, then TOTP, then success.
Call `Fail(user, now)` for unknown users too, so they lock exactly like real ones.
template: Dojo.Eq("right password, no MFA -> ok", "ok", dojoSvc.Login("ada", "ada-password", null, dojoNow));
Dojo.Eq("wrong password -> invalid", "invalid", dojoSvc.Login("ada", "nope", null, dojoNow));
Dojo.Eq("unknown user -> invalid (same answer)", "invalid", dojoSvc.Login("mallory", "x", null, dojoNow));
Dojo.Eq("MFA user without a code -> mfa_required", "mfa_required", dojoSvc.Login("grace", "grace-password", null, dojoNow));
Dojo.Eq("MFA user with a wrong code -> mfa_required", "mfa_required", dojoSvc.Login("grace", "grace-password", "000000", dojoNow));
Dojo.Eq("MFA user with the right code -> ok", "ok", dojoSvc.Login("grace", "grace-password", dojoCode, dojoNow));
Dojo.Eq("MFA user with the wrong password -> invalid, even with a good code", "invalid", dojoSvc.Login("grace", "nope", dojoCode, dojoNow));
Dojo.Eq("3 failures inside 15 minutes -> locked, even with the right password", "locked", dojoSvc.Login("ada", "ada-password", null, dojoNow.AddMinutes(3)));
Dojo.Eq("after the window passes -> ok again", "ok", dojoSvc.Login("ada", "ada-password", null, dojoNow.AddMinutes(30)));
Dojo.Eq("an unknown name locks exactly like a real one", "locked", dojoSvc.Login("mallory", "x", null, dojoNow.AddMinutes(3)));
